root_cause: af_alg_sendmsg let two writers use the same AF_ALG socket at the same time, so their data interleaved and the socket's internal state became inconsistent; the fix adds a ctx->write flag that gives one writer exclusive ownership and returns -EBUSY to a second one.
notes: Mainline fix, first in 6.17; stable backports for 5.10 to 6.16 are listed in the CVE record. Fixes: 8ff590903d5fc7f5a0a988c38267a3d08e6393a2 (algif_skcipher user-space interface, 2.6.38). For the audit, also hand over crypto/algif_skcipher.c, crypto/algif_aead.c and include/crypto/if_alg.h, which share the af_alg socket state.

root_cause: ebt_snat_tg made only the Ethernet header writable (skb_ensure_writable(skb, 0)) but then rewrote the ARP sender hardware address in place; when that range lay in a nonlinear skb fragment backed by file pages imported with splice, the write went straight into a shared page; the fix calls skb_ensure_writable over the ARP header plus the address before touching it.
notes: Mainline fix; the CVE record gives 7.1 as the first fixed mainline release and lists stable backports. Fixes: 63137bc5882a1882c553d389fdeeeace86ee1741 ('netfilter: ebtables: Fixes dropping of small packets in bridge nat').

root_cause: tls_sw_recvmsg decided whether it could keep reading records with the test `copied && control != TLS_RECORD_TYPE_DATA`; when the first record taken from rx_list had zero length, copied stayed 0 although control had been set, so a record of another type could follow in the same call and break the rule that one recvmsg returns either only DATA records or one non-DATA record; the fix tests `control && control != TLS_RECORD_TYPE_DATA`, with 0 meaning no type reported yet.
notes: Mainline fix, first in 6.17; affected from 6.0. Fixes: 84c61fe1a75b4255df1e1e7c054c9e6d048da417 ('tls: rx: do not use the standard strparser').

root_cause: nft_verdict_init accepted NF_DROP and NF_QUEUE verdicts carrying arbitrary parameters in the upper 16 bits, while nf_hook_slow reads the upper 16 bits of NF_DROP as a negative errno; a positive value such as 1 (the value of NF_ACCEPT) made nf_hook_slow free the packet and return a value its callers read as accept, leading to a double free; the fix rejects verdict parameters again.
notes: Affected 3.15 up to 6.8 per the CVE record. Fixes: e0abdadcc6e113ed2e22c85b350074487095875b ('netfilter: nf_tables: accept QUEUE/DROP verdict parameters'); the fix is effectively its revert. net/netfilter is large: if needed, narrow to nf_tables_api.c plus core.c so that both the producer (nft_verdict_init) and the consumer (nf_hook_slow) of the verdict encoding are in scope. The core.c path is from the fix commit message, not the diff.

root_cause: ovl_copy_up_one did not check that the lower file's owner uid and gid were mapped in the mounter's user namespace; for an unmapped owner copy-up neither failed nor dropped privilege, so a setuid file with capabilities copied from a nosuid mount kept those attributes in the upper layer; the fix returns -EOVERFLOW when kuid_has_mapping or kgid_has_mapping fails.
notes: Fixes: 459c7c5 ('ovl: unprivieged mounts'); Cc stable for v5.11 and later. The CVE record lists 6.2-rc6 as affected.

root_cause: Stack expansion (expand_stack and expand_downwards) changed the VMA layout while holding only the mmap read lock; since VMAs moved to the maple tree in 6.1, that write replaced tree nodes and freed the old ones through RCU while other readers under the same read lock could still use them, a use after free; the fix series always expands the stack with the mmap write lock held.
notes: Known as StackRot. Affected 6.1 to 6.4; fixed by the expand-stack series merged in 9471f1f2f502 for 6.5 and backported to 6.1.37, 6.3.11 and 6.4.1. vulnerable_ref is the merge's first parent. 8d7071af8907 ('mm: always expand the stack with the mmap write lock held') is the key commit of the series; other commits add lock_mm_and_find_vma and convert arch page-fault handlers and GUP. Paths and symbols come from the StackRot write-up and the series summary, not a line-by-line read of every patch. For the audit, also give the maple tree locking rules (lib/maple_tree.c).

root_cause: copy_page_to_iter_pipe and push_pipe filled a new pipe_buffer slot (page, offset, len, ops) without resetting flags, so a stale PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE from an earlier use of the slot let a later pipe write append data into a read-only page-cache page placed in the pipe; the fix sets buf->flags = 0 in both functions.
notes: Known as Dirty Pipe. Fixes: 241699c ('new iov_iter flavour: pipe-backed'). The fix only touches lib/iov_iter.c; fs/pipe.c (pipe_write) is where the stale merge flag is acted on, so include it in the audit.

root_cause: When a rule using an anonymous set was removed in a batch, nf_tables_deactivate_set did not move the anonymous set to the inactive state in the preparation phase, so later operations in the same batch could still reach and update the set that was already removed, a use after free at commit; the fix deactivates anonymous sets during preparation and adds nf_tables_activate_set to restore them on abort.
notes: The fix commit has no Fixes tag; the CVE record says Linux through 6.3.1. net/netfilter is large: if needed, narrow to the nf_tables core (nf_tables_api.c) and the set-using expressions (nft_lookup.c, nft_dynset.c, nft_objref.c).

root_cause: __dst_negative_advice called the protocol's negative_advice method, which released the dst entry, and only afterwards replaced sk->sk_dst_cache, against the RCU rule that the published pointer is cleared before the object is released, so the socket cache could still hand out a released entry, a use after free; the fix makes each negative_advice method clear the cache with sk_dst_reset before releasing the entry.
notes: Mainline fix, first in 6.10; affected from 4.6. Fixes: a87cb3e48ee86d29868d3f59cfb9ce1a8fa63314 ('net: Facility to report route quality of connected sockets'). The generic caller is in include/net/sock.h and the releasing methods are in the protocol files, so also give net/ipv4/route.c, net/ipv6/route.c and net/xfrm/xfrm_policy.c to the audit.

root_cause: uvc_parse_streaming sized the frames array without counting frame descriptors of formats whose frame type is UVC_VS_UNDEFINED, but uvc_parse_format still parsed and stored those frames, so the writing pass could run past the array sized by the counting pass; the fix makes uvc_parse_format skip frame parsing when the frame type is undefined.
notes: Mainline fix, first in 6.13; the bug dates back to the original driver (Fixes: c0efd232929c2cd87238de2cccdaf4e845be5b0c).

root_cause: vsock_remove_sock always called vsock_remove_bound when a transport was released, including during transport reassignment of a socket that stays alive, so the socket lost its binding and the reference that binding held while still in use, and the reference count reached zero too early, a use after free; the fix removes the binding only once the socket is dead (SOCK_DEAD) and calls sock_orphan before the transport release in __vsock_release.
notes: Mainline fix, first in 6.14. Fixes: c0cfa2d8a788fcf45df5bf4070ab2474c88d543a ('vsock: add multi-transports support').

root_cause: io_sqe_buffer_register treated the pinned pages of a fixed buffer as one physically contiguous huge-page range whenever they all belonged to the same folio, without checking that consecutive entries were adjacent pages; the same page mapped repeatedly passed that test, so accesses computed from the first page ran into the following physical pages; the fix also requires pages[i] == pages[i - 1] + 1.
notes: Fixed before 6.4-rc1. Fixes: 57bebf8 ('io_uring/rsrc: optimise registered huge pages'), which added the same-folio shortcut.

root_cause: For a provided-buffer ring registered with IOU_PBUF_RING_MMAP, the kernel allocated the ring pages and user space mapped them with mmap, but unregistering the ring (__io_remove_buffers) freed the pages at once even though user space could still have them mapped, a use after free; the fix defers freeing these pages until the io_uring context itself is freed.
notes: Affected from 6.4. Fixes: c56e022 ('io_uring: add support for user mapped provided buffer ring'). The mapping side is in io_uring/io_uring.c (mmap handler); give the whole io_uring directory.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: scalar32_min_max_and, scalar32_min_max_or and scalar32_min_max_xor left the 32-bit bounds unchanged when both 32-bit subregisters were known constants, assuming the 64-bit helper would set them, which it did only when the full 64-bit values were constant; the verifier then kept wrong 32-bit bounds and accepted programs whose run-time values fell outside them; the fix marks the 32-bit result known with __mark_reg32_known.
notes: The CVE record links the commit in the bpf tree; the same hash is in mainline (checked on the GitHub mirror). Fixed in 5.13-rc4, 5.12.4, 5.11.21 and 5.10.37 per the CVE record. Fixes: 3f50f13 ('bpf: Verifier, do explicit ALU32 bounds tracking') and 2921c90 ('bpf: Fix a verifier failure with xor').

root_cause: ieee802_11_parse_elems_full copied a nontransmitted BSSID profile into a separately allocated temporary buffer, pointed the parsed element pointers into it, and freed the buffer before returning, so callers used element pointers into freed memory; the fix keeps the scratch buffer inside the returned ieee802_11_elems structure.
notes: Affected 5.2 through 5.19.x before 5.19.16. The CVE record links the commit in the wireless tree; the same hash is in mainline (checked on the GitHub mirror). Fixes: 5023b14 ('mac80211: support profile split between elements').

root_cause: seq_read_iter kept doubling the seq_file buffer with no upper limit, and seq_dentry passed that size_t buffer size to dentry_path, which takes an int length; for a 2 GB buffer the length became negative and prepend wrote outside the buffer; the fix makes seq_buf_alloc refuse sizes above MAX_RW_COUNT.
notes: Known as Sequoia. Affected 3.16 through 5.13.x before 5.13.4. Fixes: 058504e ('fs/seq_file: fallback to vmalloc allocation'). The fix touches only fs/seq_file.c; the int-length side (dentry_path and prepend in fs/d_path.c) comes from the Qualys advisory, so also give fs/d_path.c to the audit.

root_cause: legacy_parse_param checked the room left in its one-page option buffer with `len > PAGE_SIZE - 2 - size`; with unsigned arithmetic, once size passed PAGE_SIZE - 2 the subtraction wrapped to a huge value, the check passed, and the following copy overflowed the heap buffer; the fix compares `size + len + 2 > PAGE_SIZE`.
notes: The fix commit has no Fixes tag. Reachable for file systems without native fs_context support, which fall back to the legacy parser.

root_cause: backtrack_insn did not propagate precision to both registers of a conditional jump that compares two registers, so a register whose exact value mattered for safety stayed imprecise; state pruning then judged a new state equivalent to an already verified one and skipped a path containing unsafe pointer arithmetic; the fix marks both registers of such a comparison precise.
notes: Affected 5.4 and later per the CVE record. Fixes: b5dc016 ('bpf: precise scalar_value tracking'). The pruning comparison itself (states_equal and related helpers) is in the same file.

root_cause: For IOPOLL rings, completions are committed under ctx->uring_lock without taking completion_lock, but io_commit_cqring also flushed deferred requests through io_queue_deferred, which assumes completion_lock is held; the unlocked flush could race with another and free the same io_defer_entry twice; the fix takes completion_lock around the deferred flush in io_iopoll_complete and asserts the lock in io_queue_deferred.
notes: Stable-only fix ('io_uring: ensure IOPOLL locks around deferred work') on linux-5.15.y, Cc stable for 5.10 and 5.15; the commit says there is no direct upstream commit because mainline fixed this in 5.18 as part of a completion-side rework, so do not use torvalds/linux refs. The reported device (Pixel 7) ran 5.10; the 5.10.y backport hash was not confirmed. The GitHub mirror gregkh/linux carries the same commit.

root_cause: When binder_transaction rejected a transaction before translating any object (for example because offsets_size was not aligned), its error path called binder_transaction_buffer_release with failed_at 0, which the release code read as 'release every object in the buffer', so reference counts of binder nodes named by untranslated objects were dropped, a use after free; the first fix closed that path, CVE-2023-21255 reached the same misread through another path, and bdc1c5fac982 finally separated 'no objects processed' from 'release the whole buffer'.
notes: Fix spans two CVEs. CVE-2023-20938 was reported on Android GKI 5.4 and 5.10 and fixed there in 2023-02 by backporting upstream 6d98eb95b450 ('binder: avoid potential data leakage when copying txn'), which did not remove the root cause. CVE-2023-21255 was fixed by bdc1c5fac982 ('binder: fix UAF caused by faulty buffer cleanup', Fixes: 32e9f56 'binder: don't detect sender/target during buffer cleanup'), carried in the Android common kernel as 1ca1130ec62d. The refs point at the complete fix, where the shared failed_at 0 misread is still present but only the CVE-2023-21255 path remains; a tree that shows the original CVE-2023-20938 path would be an Android common kernel 5.10 before the 2023-02 backport (ref not confirmed). Root cause wording comes from the Android Offensive Security write-up plus both commits.

root_cause: When translating 32-bit compat rules to the native layout, xt_compat_match_from_user and xt_compat_target_from_user zeroed the alignment padding after each converted match and target without checking that the padding stayed inside the allocated ruleset blob, so the zeroing could write past its end; the fix zeroes the whole new blob in translate_compat_table and removes the per-entry padding writes.
notes: Affected since 2.6.19-rc1. Fixes: 9fa492c ('[NETFILTER]: x_tables: simplify compat API'); the CVE record also links 9fa492cdc160, but that is the commit that introduced the bug, not a fix. Also give net/ipv4/netfilter/ip_tables.c (translate_compat_table) to the audit so the blob allocation is in scope.

root_cause: The driver assumed each context had at most one tracking-page VMA, but it allowed a tracking mapping larger than one page that munmap could split into several VMAs; tearing one of them down ran kbasep_os_process_page_usage_drain, which reset kctx->process_mm and finished its bookkeeping on the old mm after dropping the lock without holding a reference to it, a use after free; the fix sets process_mm at context creation, clears it at context termination and allows only single-page tracking VMAs.
audit_scope: mali_kbase driver source directory of the Bifrost/Valhall r42p0 release archive
notes: Not in torvalds/linux. Arm publishes the Mali kernel driver source as release archives, not a git repository, so repo is null and the refs are driver release versions: Bifrost r0p0-r42p0, Valhall r19p0-r42p0 and Arm 5th Gen r41p0-r42p0 affected, fixed in r43p0; Midgard r12p0-r32p0 is affected with no fixed release named. Root cause and function names come from the Google Project Zero RCA; the patch itself was not read. The path is a file name only; its directory inside the archive was not confirmed.

root_cause: nft_byteorder_eval walked 16-bit elements through pointers to a union of u32 and u16, so indexing advanced by the union's 4-byte size instead of 2 bytes and read and wrote past the end of the fixed-size register area; the fix uses plain u16 pointers for 2-byte elements and plain u32 access for 4-byte ones.
notes: Affected since 3.13-rc1. Fixes: 9651851 ('netfilter: add nftables'). The derivation record words the cause as missing bounds checks on the fixed-size registers; the patch shows the concrete cause is the 4-byte stride of the union pointer. net/netfilter is large: if needed, narrow to the nf_tables expression files (nft_*.c).

root_cause: Concurrent SMB2 SESSION_SETUP and LOGOFF requests on the same session ran without a common lock: session setup could mark a connection that needed reconnect as good again, and logoff did not look the session up again before tearing it down, so one request could keep using session state (including sess->user) that the other had freed; the fix adds connection locking around session setup, keeps the need-reconnect state, and re-validates the session in logoff.
notes: ZDI-23-698 (ZDI-CAN-20481) names this commit as the fix; the commit also lists ZDI-CAN-20590 and ZDI-CAN-20596. The derivation record words the cause as another connection binding the same session; the fix commit describes concurrent session setup and logoff. ksmbd lived in fs/ksmbd at the vulnerable ref (later moved to fs/smb/server).

root_cause: route4_change unlinked the old filter from the hash table only when `fold && fold->handle && f->handle != fold->handle`, but freed the old filter whenever one existed, so with handle 0 the freed filter stayed linked in the table, a use after free; the fix unlinks the old filter whenever it exists.
notes: Also reported as ZDI-CAN-17440 (named in the fix commit). The fix commit has no Fixes tag. net/sched is large, so the audit scope is the whole classifier file rather than the directory.

root_cause: virtio_transport_destruct freed the transport's per-socket data but left vsk->trans pointing to it, so in loopback communication vsk->trans became a dangling pointer that later code could still use, a use after free; the fix sets vsk->trans to NULL after freeing.
notes: Mainline fix, first in 6.12; affected from 4.8. Fixes: 06a8fc78367d070720af960dcecec917d3ae5f3b ('VSOCK: Introduce virtio_vsock_common.ko').

component: halo2_gadgets variable-base scalar multiplication, in the Orchard Action circuit
root_cause: In the incomplete-addition stage of variable-base scalar multiplication, double_and_add assigned the base point coordinates x_p and y_p with assign_advice; the q_mul_2 gate only kept them constant across the loop rows and no constraint tied them to the real base, so a malicious prover could run the loop on another base and bypass the Orchard diversified-address integrity check; the fix copies the base into the first loop row with copy_advice, adding a copy constraint.
notes: Fixed in halo2_gadgets 0.5.0 (tag halo2_gadgets-0.5.0 at d751768afe0d); the tag halo2_gadgets-0.4.0 still has the assign_advice lines (checked) and is an alternative vulnerable ref. The fix commit was merged through merge a101adb ('fix/varbase-mul-base-anchoring'). The fix changes the verifying key, so it adds CircuitVersion (AnchoredBase and InsecureUnanchoredBase) and needed the NU6.2 network upgrade (2026-06-03). Downstream fixed versions: orchard 0.14.0, zcash_primitives 0.28.0, zebrad 5.0.0, zcashd 6.20.0. The derivation record notes a blind test on pre-fix halo2_gadgets was proposed but not run.

root_cause: The MiMCSponge template in circomlib set its output with `outs[0] = S[nInputs - 1].xL_out;`, which assigns the signal during witness generation but adds no constraint, so a proof could use any value for the hash output; Tornado Cash built its deposit Merkle tree with this hash, so a prover could supply a forged Merkle root; the fix uses `<==`, which both assigns and constrains.
notes: The Tornado Cash write-up (the record's source) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The link between the incident and this circomlib commit ('mimcsponge: fixes assignment to outs[0]', by kobigurk, 2019-09-17) rests on secondary summaries of the write-up (bug found by Kobi Gurkan in circomlib's MiMC, fix from = to <==) and on the commit diff. The Tornado Cash contracts that used the old circuit were replaced; their addresses were not confirmed, so onchain is null.

component: Several PlonK, Bulletproofs and Girault proof implementations
root_cause: The non-interactive (Fiat-Shamir) challenge was computed from a transcript that left out public values of the statement, such as the public inputs in PlonK or a public commitment in the Girault proof, so a proof was not bound to those values and could be forged for chosen ones; the fixes add the missing public values to the transcript in both prover and verifier.
notes: Frozen Heart is a bug class that Trail of Bits disclosed across several libraries; this entry uses the SnarkJS PlonK prover and verifier as the retest target (calculateChallanges is spelled that way in the source). Other fixed instances from the disclosure: dusk-network/plonk 21143e5085de1b747f80a0cb0ea68669993ffc29 (src/proof_system/prover.rs and verifier.rs, public inputs added to the transcript); ZenGo-X/zk-paillier dc37e94f8a375a252a44a40cd3ed56e60c588937 (src/zkproofs/wi_dlog_proof.rs, CompositeDLogProof, public commitment statement.ni added to the challenge hash); ConsenSys/gnark a6369bf2b713b7829658f36e6283fe63bdaba974 (listed by Trail of Bits; it is a dependency update to gnark-crypto v0.7.0). Not fixed at disclosure: sec-bit/ckb-zkp and adjoint-io/bulletproofs; the ING zkrp repository was deleted. The disclosure names no CVE IDs.

root_cause: The BCTV14 key generation (its step 3) output extra elements in the proving parameters that the prover never uses; their presence in the published Sprout parameters let a cheating prover get around a consistency check and turn a valid proof for one statement into a proof for another; Zcash removed the problem by moving to Groth16 with new parameters in the Sapling network upgrade.
notes: Question-level test only. The flaw is in the published BCTV14 scheme and the Sprout parameters from the 2016 ceremony, not in one code change; it was removed by the Sapling network upgrade (block 419,200, 2018-10-28), so there is no single fix commit or vulnerable ref. The Electric Coin Co. announcement says other BCTV14 implementations such as libsnark and snarkjs were affected. libsnark's generator is r1cs_ppzksnark_generator in libsnark/zk_proof_systems/ppzksnark/r1cs_ppzksnark/r1cs_ppzksnark.tcc (scipr-lab/libsnark), a possible code target, but whether that code emits the extra elements was not confirmed.

root_cause: Transaction validation accepted key images without checking that they lie in the prime-order subgroup of ed25519; because the curve has cofactor 8, adding a small-order point gave the same output several distinct valid key images, which defeated the one-key-image-per-output double-spend check; the fix rejects any key image whose product with the curve order l is not the identity.
notes: The same flaw affected other CryptoNote-based coins; this entry uses Monero as the retest target. The fix ('core: test key images against validity domain') adds core::check_tx_inputs_keyimages_domain next to the existing duplicate key image check in core::check_tx_semantic, and adds the curve order constant in src/ringct/rctOps.h. Per the disclosure it shipped in v0.10.2 (2017-02-22), with a hard fork on 2017-04-14 for full network protection. PR #1744 also carries unrelated update-checking commits.

root_cause: To avoid a costly check during block validation, CheckBlock called CheckTransaction with fCheckDuplicateInputs set to false, so a transaction that spent the same input twice was not rejected there; later code hit an assertion (node crash) and, from 0.15 on, could let the same output be spent twice and inflate supply; the fix passes true again.
notes: Introduced by PR #9049 in 0.14.0; affected 0.14.0 through 0.16.2; fixed in 0.16.3 and 0.17.0rc4. The inflation impact applies from 0.15. Also give src/consensus/tx_verify.cpp (CheckTransaction and its fCheckDuplicateInputs parameter) to the audit.

root_cause: Transaction checks did not bound each output value or the running totals of outputs and inputs, so adding two huge outputs overflowed the signed 64-bit sum to a negative value that passed the inputs-cover-outputs check; the fix adds MAX_MONEY (21 million coins) and rejects outputs and input totals above it in CheckTransaction and ConnectInputs.
notes: Value overflow incident in block 74638 on 2010-08-15; the patched client was released the same day and the chain was reorganized by block 74691. The early history is an import of the SourceForge SVN repository, and at this commit the source files sit at the repository root, so the audit scope is the whole tree (about the size of one session; narrow to main.h and main.cpp if needed). The fix also touches serialize.h.
